speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you've had fatigue, flank pain, and fever following antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis. To confirm if this is a kidney infection, have you noticed burning with urination or frequent urges to urinate? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Leukocyturia: Present; Bacterial_Culture: Negative; Cytospin_Stained_With_Hansel's_Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis confirms inflammation with white blood cells, but the negative bacterial culture and the presence of binucleated eosinophils suggest an allergic reaction rather than a bacterial kidney infection. Given your recent treatment for sinusitis, do you have a history of allergies or asthma, and have you experienced itching or a rash? REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of binucleated eosinophils in your urine and the worsening of symptoms after antibiotic treatment strongly suggests an allergic reaction, possibly interstitial nephritis. Have you noticed any hives, itchy skin, or swelling? REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: That reaction pattern—rash appearing with amoxicillin and resolving after switching to cephalexin, only to return or symptoms persisting—raises suspicion for a specific antibiotic allergy or a re-exposure issue. Did you accidentally take cephalexin again recently, or are you currently on a different antibiotic now? Also, does the rash itch intensely, and have you had any new medications besides antibiotics? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine; REQUEST TEST: Serum_IgE

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Creatinine: Elevated; IgE: Not Available

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated creatinine confirms significant kidney injury, likely acute interstitial nephritis given the eosinophilia and your reaction to antibiotics. Since we have not yet requested imaging, I am asking for it to visualize any renal structural changes or edema. REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of urinary symptoms like burning or color changes, combined with your eosinophilic findings, elevated creatinine, and specific reaction to antibiotics, strongly points to Acute Interstitial Nephritis. I have requested the ultrasound; once we review the images, will you confirm if you have a history of asthma or allergies to penicillins or cephalosporins?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
